article.title: Why Average Purchase Frequency Can Rise Even When Nobody Shops More Often

paragraphs.en:
An average can change even when the behavior of every continuing customer stays exactly the same. This is especially important when analysts compare purchase frequency across years.

Imagine a retailer with three customers. Customer A shops 12 times a year, B shops 6 times, and C shops 2 times. Their average frequency is about 6.7 visits. Next year, A still shops 12 times and B still shops 6 times, but C leaves completely. Among the remaining customers, average frequency becomes 9 visits. The average has increased sharply, although nobody who stayed is shopping more often.

This is a composition effect. The population used to calculate the average has changed. Low-frequency customers disappeared, so the remaining group is mechanically more active on average. If a dashboard simply reports “average frequency increased 34%,” a reader may incorrectly conclude that an engagement program made customers visit more often.

A useful analysis separates two questions. First, did the composition of customers change? Compare the shares of low-, medium-, and high-frequency customers, new customers, and customers who left. Second, did the same customers change their behavior? A common-customer or fixed-cohort analysis compares people observed in both periods.

Neither view is sufficient by itself. A fixed cohort can reveal within-customer change, but it excludes acquisition and churn, which may be economically important. A full-population view captures the business as it actually exists, but its averages mix behavioral change with population change. Reporting both gives a more complete explanation.

The same issue appears in spending, conversion, product usage, and employee performance. Suppose low-spending customers leave while high-spending customers remain. Average spend per customer can rise even if every remaining customer spends the same amount. Similarly, a product’s average sessions per active user can rise because casual users stop returning.

Analysts should therefore be careful with language. Instead of saying, “Customers are visiting more often,” say, “Average frequency among active customers increased, partly because the customer mix changed.” Then quantify the within-customer change separately.

A practical decomposition can start with four numbers: total customers, retained customers, average frequency for the full population, and average frequency for customers present in both periods. Add frequency bands if the audience needs more detail. These measures help distinguish stronger behavior from selective retention.

It is also useful to show the size of each group. If the common-customer group represents only half of this year's customers, its behavioral trend should not be presented as the whole business story. New customers may have naturally lower frequency because they were observed for fewer months, so exposure time should also be aligned when necessary.

The broader lesson is that averages describe a population, not a fixed person. When the population changes, the average can move without individual behavior moving in the same direction. Before explaining an average as behavioral improvement, ask who entered, who left, how long each person was observable, and whether the same people actually changed.
paragraphs.zh:
平均值會因母體組成改變而移動，即使每一位持續顧客的行為完全沒變。例如果低頻顧客離開，剩下高頻顧客，平均來店頻率就會上升。這是 composition effect，而不一定是 engagement 改善。

分析時應拆成兩個問題：客群構成是否改變，以及同一批顧客的行為是否改變。全體母體能反映實際 business mix，但會混合流入、流失與個人行為變化；common-customer/fixed cohort 則能觀察 within-customer change，卻會排除 acquisition 與 churn。兩者都應呈現。

實務上可同時列出總顧客數、retained customers、全體平均頻率、共同顧客平均頻率，再視需要加入頻率帶。若新客觀察月份較短，也要處理 exposure time。報告時不要直接說「顧客來得更頻繁」，而應說「active customers 的平均頻率上升，其中一部分來自 customer mix 改變」，再另外量化同一顧客的變化。
paragraphs.ja:
平均値は、継続顧客一人ひとりの行動が変わっていなくても、母集団の構成が変わるだけで動きます。低頻度顧客が離脱し、高頻度顧客が残れば、残存顧客の平均利用回数は機械的に上昇します。これは composition effect であり、必ずしもエンゲージメント改善を意味しません。

分析では「顧客構成が変わったか」と「同じ顧客の行動が変わったか」を分けます。全顧客ベースは実際の事業構成を反映しますが、流入・離脱と行動変化が混ざります。共通顧客や固定 cohort の比較は個人内変化を見やすい一方、新規獲得や離脱を除外します。

実務では総顧客数、継続顧客数、全体平均頻度、共通顧客の平均頻度をセットで示すと説明しやすくなります。新規顧客の観測期間が短い場合は exposure time にも注意が必要です。「顧客の来店が増えた」と断定せず、「平均頻度は上昇したが、一部は顧客構成の変化による」と表現し、個人内変化を別途示すのが正確です。

vocabulary.usage: The average rises mechanically when low-frequency users leave.
Use a fixed cohort to study within-customer change.
A decomposition separates mix from behavior.
Align exposure time for new customers.

business.term: Is this a mix effect or a behavioral change?
business.explanation: 用來區分構成變化與個人行為變化。

business.term: Let's compare the common-customer cohort separately.
business.explanation: 提議用共同 cohort 驗證 within-customer change。
